newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says cost of Spanish strike disruption unclear.
newsitem.headline: VW says cost of Spanish strike disruption unclear.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Friday it was too early to gauge to full impact of the production stoppages caused by the Spanish truckers' strike, but conceded the situation could worsen.

VW, like rival German carmakers, has been forced to shorten shifts at its main plant in Wolfsburg from next week because essential materials are not making their way through Spain's clogged-up motorways.
Daimler-Benz AG and General Motors unit Adam Opel AG are planning similar steps as the impact of the nine-day old strike by some 300,000 Spanish truckers hits home.
A Volkswagen spokesman said it was still unclear whether output would have to be reduced at other German plants as well as Wolfsburg, which usually produces some 3,000 Polo and Golf model cars daily.
If the situation did not ease, Spanish business might also have to be interrupted. At present, strong efforts were being made to seek alternative means to transport supplies.
Some 20,000 workers stand to be affected by stoppages at VW's Wolfsburg plant.

Earlier, Volkswagen said it had suspended all special shifts to try to keep the plant open on Monday and had made a precautionary request at unemployment offices to pay out compensation to workers whose shifts will be pared back.
"At the moment it does not look like the situation will change at all," said spokesman Hans-Juergen Uhl.

Rival Daimler-Benz also said the strike had affected its plant in Vitoria, Spain where some 625 vehicles could not be built because of inadequate supplies but that the impact had not yet affected operations in Germany.
Two days ago, Adam Opel AG, a unit of General Motors said it would interrupt production of its Vectra model at its Ruesselsheim plant from today.
BMW said on Friday that it had not yet been affected by the strike but was anticipating problems if it goes on much longer.
